solution:
**Note:** As printed both \(\text{NH}_3\) and \(\text{Cl}^-\) act as Bronsted bases in this reaction. The answer shown follows the paper's key, (A).

A Bronsted base accepts a proton. \(\text{NH}_3\) accepts one from HCl in the forward reaction, and \(\text{Cl}^-\) accepts one from \(\text{NH}_4^+\) in the reverse reaction. Option A.

**Note:** Sodium propanoate with soda-lime gives ethane, which the printed options do not list. The paper's key is (b), printed as ethene and meant as ethane.

Soda-lime removes the \(-\text{COONa}\) group of sodium propanoate (\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COONa}\)) as \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\), leaving ethane, \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\). Option B.
